problem_statement: yasser-acc/Portfolio-websites-templates is Ansel Thorne's static furniture-studio portfolio (a Bootstrap-derived template) served straight from index.html plus a blog-single.html article page, styled by css/style.css. The home page has a hero, an About block, a services carousel, a 'Selected Work' project grid with category filter tabs (all / seating / tables / cabinets / restoration / commissions), a 'From the Workshop' journal, a contact form and a shared footer; blog-single.html reuses the same navigation and footer. The 'Selected Work' grid is the studio's own portfolio browser and already ships with an isotope filter (js/main.js) that re-filters the six project cards by category. Deliver three coordinated things while preserving the warm Ansel Thorne studio look: (1) REPAIR the 'Selected Work' filter tab row so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow (the tab row currently is a fixed non-wrapping row that pushes the whole page sideways); do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden — the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width, so the tabs must wrap. (2) Give the project grid a real result-count status bar and carry the SAME grid+filter feature onto the blog-single.html article page as a compact 'More from the workshop' strip, styled to match the warm studio editorial language (parchment card frames, warm-brown active-tab treatment) — the grid must render faithfully to the reference (clean rows of card thumbnails, a legible active tab), not as overlapping/broken columns or an illegible active tab. (3) Wire the filter end to end: clicking a category tab (e.g. seating) must re-filter the cards AND update the result-count status bar to 'Showing N of 6 · <Category>' (e.g. 'Showing 3 of 6 · Seating') — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected category, not the default 'Showing 6 of 6 · All work'. Keep the hero, About, services, the six portfolio pieces, the journal, the contact form, the navigation and desktop/tablet layout intact.
required_content: The 'Selected Work' filter tab row (all / seating / tables / cabinets / restoration / commissions) keeps its six category tabs and renders within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px (the tabs wrap instead of forcing a fixed non-wrapping row).

The project grid shows a result-count status bar ('Showing 6 of 6 · All work' by default), and the SAME grid+filter feature also appears on the blog-single.html article page as a 'More from the workshop' strip — the shared feature on both pages, not only on the home page.

The 'Selected Work' project grid renders faithfully to the reference: clean rows of parchment-framed card thumbnails with a legible warm-brown active filter tab — not the six cards forced into one overlapping/broken row and not an illegible near-black-on-near-black active tab.

The category filter is wired end to end: clicking a tab re-filters the cards AND updates the result-count status bar to 'Showing N of 6 · <Category>' (e.g. clicking seating sets 'Showing 3 of 6 · Seating'); the post-click terminal state reflects the selected category, not the default 'Showing 6 of 6 · All work'.
The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports.

The hero, About block, services carousel, the six portfolio pieces, the journal, the contact form and the shared navigation/footer remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font errors).
design_constraints: Fix the responsive layout of the 'Selected Work' filter tab row so it wraps within a 390px phone; do not delete the tabs, change the six categories, or restyle unrelated sections.

Add a real result-count status bar to the project grid and carry the SAME grid+filter feature onto blog-single.html as a 'More from the workshop' strip so the portfolio browser is consistent across the site; do not add it to only one page.

Preserve the Ansel Thorne studio design language: warm neutral palette, serif/clean type, the services/portfolio/journal rhythm, the existing navigation and footer; the grid cards and active filter tab must render in the warm parchment/brown editorial palette and stay legible.
Keep the filter interaction wired end to end (clicking a tab must re-filter the cards and the result-count status bar must reflect the clicked category), not merely a class toggle.
Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console.
state_constraints: The home states (desktop, mobile, tablet) capture the scrolled-to-top hero; the restyle must land the Ansel Thorne name and furniture-maker tagline above the fold on desktop_home.
desktop_about, desktop_services, desktop_portfolio, and desktop_contact scroll to #about, #services, #portfolio, and #contact so each restyled section is captured in place on the single page.
desktop_blog captures the blog-single.html article, which must read as a productized furniture-craft post rather than the Lorem-ipsum demo.
Source inspection confirms the site is a static Bootstrap portfolio served directly with many local portfolio/blog/avatar images that the demo underuses semantically.

change_completion: The 'Selected Work' filter tab row renders within the viewport on a 390px phone.
The project grid shows a result-count status bar and the same grid+filter feature appears on the home AND blog pages.
Clicking a category tab updates the result-count status bar to the selected category.
design_consistency: The Ansel Thorne palette, section rhythm, navigation and footer are preserved.
The project grid renders faithfully (clean card rows, legible active tab) and matches the warm studio look across both pages.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a filter tab re-filters the cards and updates the result-count status bar to the selected category (post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
regression: Hero, About, services, portfolio, journal, contact form and navigation/footer remain reachable and unchanged.
The static site serves from index.html / blog-single.html with a clean browser console.
responsive: On a 390px mobile phone the home page (initial + portfolio) has no horizontal overflow beyond 24px, and the 834px tablet layout stays within its viewport.
The filter tab row is responsive: the tabs wrap cleanly on mobile instead of forcing a fixed-width non-wrapping row that overflows the phone viewport.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static-portfolio task REBUILT to true-new-L4 on the Ansel Thorne furniture-studio template (index.html + blog-single.html). The lever is the portfolio's OWN 'Selected Work' project grid and its native isotope category filter — not a bolted-on metric rail. The reference (a) repairs the filter tab row so it wraps within a 390px phone (fixed non-wrapping row -> wrapping flex), (b) adds a real result-count status bar to the grid and carries the SAME grid+filter feature onto the blog page as a 'More from the workshop' strip in the warm parchment/brown studio palette, and (c) wires the filter so the count status bar reflects the clicked category. The bad 'smart-wrong' solution narrows the tab row to min-width:560px + an inner overflow-x:hidden non-fix (document still overflows -> D6 fail), adds the grid feature to the home page only (cross-PAGE D2 fail on the blog page), forces the six project cards into one overlapping non-wrapping row with a near-black-on-near-black illegible active tab (D3 visual_regression fail), and flips the active tab + isotope re-filters but never re-syncs the count status bar (click succeeds but the terminal readout stays 'Showing 6 of 6 · All work' -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). It fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. The template's body{overflow-x:hidden} was neutralized as declared INFRA identical across all three legs so the real document overflow is measurable. The baseline leg carries the original layout defect (D6+D3) and lacks the blog-page grid (D2) but its filter count-sync JS is byte-identical to the reference, so baseline PASSES D4 (leg-orthogonal).
